title: smart-routing-fallback-debug-notes-ryan
content:
Quick notes / breadcrumbs while debugging the EU regional failover issue (obs on 2025-11-03 -> elevated 11/04). Personal scratchpad - rough, incomplete.

Summary:
- Symptom: customer traffic to eu-west1 (prod) got elevated 503/504s starting ~2025-11-03 02:10 UTC. Smart routing did NOT trigger expected fallback to eu-west1-readonly or us-west1 as per fallback policy.
- Immediate impact: subset of tenant requests experienced 80% error rate for ~18m before partial mitigation.
- Hypothesis (working): stale routing table entries + incorrect healthcheck aggregation allowed routes to remain marked as healthy even though downstream inference instances were starving (OOM or queue saturation).

Timeline / actions taken:
- 2025-11-03 02:12 UTC: Pager -> I joined call. Observed spike in 503s in product dashboard for region eu-west1.
- 02:14 UTC: Query routing table for tenant X: 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEBUG_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/v1/routes?tenant=X | jq '.routes[] | select(.region=="eu-west1")'
  Output: route_id=rt-87, state=ACTIVE, health=OK, last_health_check=2025-11-03T02:09:58Z
  Note: last_health_check is stale relative to error start time.
- 02:16 UTC: Check instance health in eu-west1 cluster: 
  kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference,region=eu-west1 -o wide
  Output: several pods in CrashLoopBackOff (OOMKilled) and some Ready=0/1.
- 02:17 UTC: Fetch pod logs for one failing replica: 
  kubectl -n inference logs inference-xyz -c inference-runtime | tail -n 200
  Snippets: "Failed to allocate KV cache chunk: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory"
  And: "batch_queue length=2048, processing_latency_ms 12000, dropping request"
- 02:20 UTC: re-check control plane health aggregation: 
  curl -s https://controlplane.internal/v1/health/aggregate?region=eu-west1 | jq
  Output: "healthy_instances": 18, "monitoring_delay_ms": 3500
  But node exporter shows many nodes reporting stale metrics (prometheus scrape gap).
- 02:25 UTC: Tried forcing fallback for tenant X via admin API (temporary mitigation): 
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"tenant":"X","force_fallback":"us-west1"}' https://controlplane.internal/v1/admin/route/force
  Result: routes switched to us-west1 and error rate dropped to ~2% within ~45s.
- 02:40 UTC: rolled back forced fallback after autoscale and pod restarts showed recovery.

Commands/queries I ran (raw) - saved for runbook additions:
- curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEBUG_TOKEN" https://controlplane.internal/v1/routes?tenant=X | jq '.'
- kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference,region=eu-west1 -o wide
- kubectl -n inference logs $POD -c inference-runtime --previous | grep -E 'OOMKilled|cudaMalloc|batch_queue' -n -C 3
- curl -s https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query_range?query=avg_over_time(inference_batch_queue_length[5m])&start=...
- kubectl -n controlplane logs controlplane-0 | grep -E 'health-aggregation|route-state-change'

Error snippets (copied raw):
- "2025-11-03T02:13:24Z inference-runtime ERROR Failed to allocate KV cache chunk: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory"
- "2025-11-03T02:15:01Z router WARN route rt-87 health_check_timeout (last ok 2025-11-03T02:09:58Z)"
- "2025-11-03T02:15:05Z controlplane INFO health-aggregator: region=eu-west1 healthy=18 scrapes=0 delayed=3200ms"
- "2025-11-03T02:16:47Z inference-runtime WARN batch_queue length=2048 latency_ms=12000 dropping=120"

Observations / correlating signals:
- Many inference pods OOM or high memory pressure -> suggests memory leak or quantization mismatch after last model rollout (PR #418 referenced below).
- Control plane health aggregation has a scrape/latency window of ~3s; but dashboards indicate Prometheus scrape gaps (10-15s) during incident which may have caused health aggregator to see stale health as OK.
- Fallback policy triggers when controlplane marks region unhealthy AND route-level failure rate > threshold. Here controlplane health remained (misleadingly) OK due to stale metrics, so fallback didn't trigger automatically.
- Autoscaler had signalled desired replicas=50 but cluster had only 12 ready due to OOMs and crashloops -> capacity mismatch.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Recent routing/config change (PR #418) changed model/quantization selection logic for eu-west1, increasing memory per replica -> OOMs under normal load. This caused pod instability but health aggregator wasn't catching it quickly.
2) Health-aggregator relies on Prometheus scrape timestamps; if scrapes are delayed (prometheus OOM?), aggregator treats last known metric as fresh for too long (TTL bug).
3) Circuit breaker / fallback policy gating condition incorrectly requires BOTH health=false AND route_error_rate>threshold; in transient saturation route_error_rate lags behind internal metrics, delaying fallback.

Intermediate reproduction attempts (local / staging):
- Rolled the new config in staging with a synthetic load (rps=250) and observed memory climb and eventual OOM within 12 minutes. Reproduces in staging with same model build.
- Instrumented runtime to dump KV-cache allocations on warn; confirmed allocation spikes aligning with large batched requests.

Mitigations applied during incident:
- Force-fallback to us-west1 for heavily-affected tenants (manual admin API).
- Disabled PR#418 model-selection flag for eu-west1 via feature-flag service (partial rollback).
- Scaled cluster nodes up (added 8 nodes) to reduce immediate pressure while rolling restarts.

Proposed fixes / next steps (short list):
- Roll back PR #418 for all regions until we confirm memory profile (owner: @olivia).
- Fix health-aggregator TTL handling: reduce grace-window and use last_scrape_timestamp delta rather than heuristic (owner: eng-sre).
- Add a fast-path fallback: if a majority of pods in region are CrashLoopBackOff or Ready<50%, trigger fallback immediately (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
- Tune circuit-breaker logic to use streaming error rate (short-window) rather than 5m average to avoid delayed fallbacks.
- Add an automated smoke-check during rollouts that applies a small synthetic load and validates memory/P95 latency before promoting (owner: release-engineering).

Runbook additions (to create):
- Exact admin API commands for forced fallback and how to undo.
- Checklist: check prometheus scrape latency, controlplane health-agg last_scrape, pod Ready counts, autoscaler desired vs ready, force fallback steps, rollback flag steps.

Notes for postmortem:
- Timeline of when controlplane decisions allowed traffic to keep flowing into a degraded region.
- What telemetry gaps allowed health aggregator to be misled.
- Whether release PR changed memory profile (binary diff + perf profile).

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Is the memory regression from model binary (weights/quant) or from runtime change? (Next: bisect model builds between last known-good and current.)
- Did autoscaler metrics come from stale metrics source? I saw desired replicas=50 from scaler but actual node pool not matching. Need to pull cluster autoscaler logs.
- Owner assignments: confirm Olivia will revert PR#418 in the morning.

Last raw artifacts saved to bucket: gs://debug-scrap/eu-fallback-20251103/{prometheus-snap.json,controlplane-logs.tgz,pod-logs-eu.tgz}

If anyone picks this up: start with 1) verify PR#418 rollback in staging, 2) apply TTL fix in a canary controlplane, 3) add fast-path region-unhealthy rule. I can help with follow-up repros and telemetry queries.

-- Ryan

(quick note: keep this doc internal; will move cleaned notes to postmortem draft in confluence after call)
